image_description:
## 1) Chart type
- **Left panel:** Multi-series **line chart**
- **Right panel:** **Stacked area chart**

## 2) Layout techniques
- The visualization uses **two side-by-side panels**.
- The **left panel** compares major greenhouse gas source sectors with multiple lines, with **transportation highlighted by color** and others muted.
- The **right panel** provides a **breakdown of transportation emissions** using **stacking** in an area chart.
- This is a **drill-down / decomposition layout**, not a faceted grid or small multiples.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Year (1990–2017) | Temporal | Position on x-axis (both panels) |
| Greenhouse gas emissions (billion metric tons / metric tons) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis (left panel); stacked area height / y-extent (right panel) |
| Source sector (e.g., Electricity, Transportation, Industry, Agriculture, others) | Categorical/nominal | Separate lines; color/hue emphasis; direct text labels (left panel) |
| Transportation subcategory (e.g., Passenger Vehicles, Trucks, Trains/planes/ships/other) | Categorical/nominal | Stacked areas; color/hue; direct text labels (right panel) |

Today’s graphs show the change in the amount of greenhouse gases emissions by industry and by type of transportation.  (How does Thanksgiving travel relate to these graphs?)

From 9 am – 2 pm E.T. today, share with us your responses online to these three questions -- "What do you notice?",  "What do you wonder?", and  "What's going on in this graph?"  

Plus, please share with us a catchy headline that captures the ideas about the graphs. 

On Thursday afternoon, we’ll reveal the article that included these graphs and much more.  We look forward to reading your discoveries.

The next “What’s Going On in This Graph?” will be moderated on Wednesday, December 4.  The topic – immigrants and crime.  In the meantime, have a wonderful Thanksgiving holiday.
